verdict: MetLife's GAAP profit nearly tripled to $2.4B as premiums jumped 12% and its hedges swung from a $929M loss to a $698M gain; the steadier adjusted EPS rose 17% to $2.78.

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: What policyholders pay for life, disability, dental and other coverage — up 12%, helped by pension risk-transfer deals (taking over companies' pension promises).

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the huge portfolio MetLife invests between collecting premiums and paying claims.

segments.name: Policy fees
segments.note: Fees charged on universal life and investment-type policies.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Everything else MetLife books as revenue.

segments.name: Investment & derivative results, net
segments.note: A $698M gain on derivatives (hedges that rise when markets fall) minus $430M of net investment losses — these market-driven lines swing wildly quarter to quarter.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Running the company: staff, technology and operations, net of amounts capitalized into DAC (deferred acquisition costs).

opex.name: Amortization of DAC & VOBA
opex.note: Spreading the upfront cost of winning policies (commissions and underwriting) over the policies' lives.

otherDetail: All non-operating market items already sit inside revenue and claims lines for an insurer; below pre-tax profit, $588M of tax, $15M to noncontrolling interests and $46M of preferred dividends leave $2,351M for common shareholders.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Premiums drove real growth
takeaways.text: Premiums rose 12% to $11.8B, helped by pension risk-transfer business — MetLife taking over pension obligations from employers — and solid group benefits sales.

takeaways.title: Hedges explain the GAAP jump
takeaways.text: Derivative gains of $698M replaced a $929M loss a year ago. These hedges protect the balance sheet, but they make GAAP profit swing hard; adjusted EPS (+17%) is the calmer gauge.

takeaways.title: Adjusted earnings rose steadily
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS of $2.78 rose 17% year over year — the number management steers by, because it removes investment and derivative noise.

footerNote: For an insurer, 'cost of revenue' here is the claims block: $11,474M of policyholder benefits and claims, $2,201M of interest credited to policyholder accounts, $136M of policyholder dividends and $182M net of liability and market-risk-benefit remeasurement losses. MetLife's segment revenues are not broken out in its release, so the chart's sources are its revenue lines. Net income was $2,412M; the $2,351M shown is what remained for common shareholders after noncontrolling interests and preferred dividends.
